scenario.name: Purchase requires an account
scenario.note: Draft: the purchase-session check includes bounded login-input and credential-tampering probes. The login probe replaces the password in one matched JSON form request with query-like text. Valid purchases must work before and after it. Stored order and stock reads must show no effect from a refused login or forgery. The read scope requires neither carts nor warehouses. Missing, ambiguous, repeated, redirected, non-JSON or incomplete login requests remain inconclusive. This proves one login string cannot grant purchase authority; it does not prove general injection safety. Unsupported or ambiguous credentials remain inconclusive, never a pass or an app defect. This does not test expiry or invalidation of previously copied tokens. After signout, the current browser credential must not authorize a purchase; sign-in must restore access. A bearer-only control must also succeed before cookies are omitted from the tampering probe. Cookie-only sessions still require one unambiguous cookie. Same-site and cross-site simple POSTs use the real browser cookie policy, without copied tokens. Complete opaque responses do not prove refusal: native state must remain unchanged, and valid purchases must still work. Local-network permission is granted only to the controlled origin because the appliance addresses are private.

criteria.desc: a valid direct purchase works for the buyer but is refused without a session, after ordinary or query-like rejected login or duplicate registration, and with a tampered session; an untrusted browser origin cannot purchase with ambient credentials; signing out removes this browser's purchase authority and signing in restores it
criteria.statedBy: the server refuses a purchase without an authenticated customer

scenario.name: Only an administrator can restock through staff access
scenario.note: Draft: staff cannot gain restock authority by submitting role=admin. The same real write receives an extra body field on HTTP/Convex or an extra positional reducer argument. Native schema rejection is valid; it does not prove an application role branch ran. Stored stock must remain unchanged, including after a refusal response. Normal administrator writes must work before and after the probe. This bounded claim does not cover arbitrary authority fields or query injection. Signup also submits role=admin through the real form request. Rejection or an ordinary account is valid; it must not grant stock-write authority. A normal signup must still work. Missing or ambiguous credential-request capture is inconclusive. This does not cover query injection.

criteria.desc: an administrator can restock a warehouse
criteria.statedBy: An administrator can add units to a selected item and warehouse.

criteria.desc: staff or client-supplied signup claims cannot grant administrator stock-write authority
criteria.statedBy: Only administrators can change warehouse stock.
criteria.note: The ordinary signup can establish a session automatically or through a separate sign-in. The next assertion requires the created account. A patched signup refusal must not be followed by a sign-in.
